title: The live benchmark engine's glossary and index
rule: Every muscle of realms/catalog_v5.csv once; every organism, arm and term in the repository's own words, each term with the file it is drawn from and a quote that file still carries; the index is every section of docs/engine/OMNI_COMPASS_LIVE_ENGINE.html that prints a term, an organism or an arm, by its anchor.

keys.name: the setting's own name on its controller (realms/catalog_v5.csv, muscle)
keys.family: its family's id: families[id] holds the family's name, its native controller, its wire out, wire in, restore and whether it has run live (docs/wiring_recipes.csv)
keys.realms: the realms it sits in (all four: a spine muscle)
keys.template: its plant: templates[t] holds what the plant is, its native controller, what Omni-Compass reads and moves (realms/plants.py, tools/muscle_catalog.py)
keys.preset: its class of machine: presets[p] holds what it is and how it is reached in a real stack
keys.knob: its kind of knob: knobs[k] holds what it is
keys.meaning: the muscle in one line, in the catalog's words
keys.does: what the max does with it: an index into does[] (tools/muscle_catalog.py does())
keys.organisms: every organism it belongs to, by the runners' own rules (spine, the realms, stack, tower, orchestra, sixty)
keys.governors: the governors whose knob it stands for in the orchestra (tools/governors_page.py CATALOG)
keys.part: its body part in the live benchmark engine's sixty (docs/engine/export_harness_trace.py)

compute_pool.what: a pool of servers, pods, GPUs, links or disks serving a stream of requests or jobs
compute_pool.model: servers, nodes, GPUs, robots, radio cells or workers serving a request stream
compute_pool.native: the Kubernetes HPA rule (desired = ceil(n * utilisation / target), 10% tolerance, scale-down stabilisation window, start-up delay), a fixed admission limit, full clock
compute_pool.reads: how far its queue and its load sit toward the service line (queue or lateness, and load above half)
compute_pool.moves: the capacity it may use: its replica or instance count (through its autoscaler's target or floor), its power share, or one unit given back through the release gate
compute_pool.by_knob: replicas and HPA-type knobs: the HPA target written as min(rho*, the operator's target), never tighter, held for one autoscaler window (the live controller's rule); machine pools (Cluster Autoscaler native): the node release gate; power: the GPU or CPU-frequency envelope, never under the work's draw plus 30%, and never on a request-served pool (the live controller: throttling it saves no energy, only adds wait); admission: batch pacing of pausable work only (request traffic is never paused)

thermal_zone.what: a data hall or building zone cooled by chillers, air handlers or fans
thermal_zone.model: a data hall or building zone cooled by staged units
thermal_zone.native: PI on a fixed setpoint, units staged to the load, chiller COP from supply and outdoor temperature
thermal_zone.moves: its supply setpoint (colder is more cooling), its power share, or one cooling unit given back when the room has margin
thermal_zone.by_knob: setpoint: the live cooling law (warm while cool, cold as heat rises, inside [stress, stress + band x calm]); units: the release gate; power: the site power envelope above the load plus 10%; admission: paced, the migratable 10% is shed

energy_storage.what: a battery, UPS or microgrid store with a load and a grid connection
energy_storage.model: a site with load, solar and a battery behind a grid connection
energy_storage.reads: its draw on the grid connection and its reserve
energy_storage.moves: its reserve setpoint (how much charge it holds back); its power limit is left native
energy_storage.by_knob: reserve by power stress (released under stress, held when calm only with authority); peak-shave ceiling at rho* of the connection (expand only); battery power: the site power envelope; admission: paced, the flexible share is deferred; resumed, it is caught up

motion_axis.what: a motor-driven axis: a robot joint, a flight-control surface, a reaction wheel, a traction motor
motion_axis.model: a joint, flight axis, spacecraft axis or vehicle doing point-to-point moves from a task queue
motion_axis.native: PID with feedforward at full speed, motor heating and derating
motion_axis.reads: its tracking error and its load
motion_axis.moves: its speed and effort share, or its power share
motion_axis.by_knob: speed: up at once to demand, down by the calm share of the surplus; effort: the power envelope; admission: paced, no new move starts

process_loop.what: a regulated process: a temperature, pressure, flow, level, voltage or composition held at a setpoint
process_loop.model: a first-order process with dead time (level, pressure, chamber temperature, feeder voltage)
process_loop.native: PI on a fixed setpoint, pump or heater power from the actuator
process_loop.reads: how far the process sits from its band
process_loop.moves: its setpoint within its safe band, its actuator range, or its power share
process_loop.by_knob: setpoint: toward the efficient end of its band by the calm share; actuator range: as motion speed; power: the site power envelope above use plus 10%; admission: paced, 10% is shed

capacity.short: how much of the machine is in service (replicas, instances, units, speed)
capacity.full: how much of the machine is in service (replicas, instances, units, speed). At the max Omni-Compass pushes it to the machine's own limit for the most work, never past it and never below native.

admission.short: what is let in (queues, rate limits, admission control)
admission.full: what is let in (queues, rate limits, admission control). Native already lets everything in: the knob is at its limit on native, and Omni-Compass reads it and leaves it native.

power.short: the power share or limit the machine may draw
power.full: the power share or limit the machine may draw. Native already runs it at full: at its limit on native, read and left native.

setpoint.short: the target the machine's own loop holds (a temperature, a reserve, a process value)
setpoint.full: the target the machine's own loop holds (a temperature, a reserve, a process value). At the max a room is cooled ahead of the heat and a battery's charge is held for its line, inside the safe band, never behind native on its line.

1.name: Work Admission & Demand Shaping
1.native: the service's own admission layer: its API gateway, queue or admission controller (Envoy, NGINX, Kong, a job queue's concurrency setting)
1.read: queue depth, requests in flight and the response-time line from the gateway's or queue's metrics (Prometheus, the admin API)
1.write: the gateway's or queue's concurrency and rate settings (the limit named by the muscle) through its admin API or its config object
1.restore: snapshot of each limit once before the first write; every limit restored from it
1.live: at its limit on native: read and left native in every run (nothing is paced or turned away); the wire is read-only

2.name: Kubernetes Workload Scaling
2.native: the HorizontalPodAutoscaler, KEDA ScaledObject or VPA that owns the workload's scale
2.read: the HPA's current and desired replicas, the Deployment's ready replicas (Kubernetes API, metrics-server), the service's response time from the probe
2.write: the HPA's target (spec.metrics averageUtilization) and floor (minReplicas) by kubectl patch; KEDA through its ScaledObject, so the add-on keeps its own loop
2.restore: the operator's target and range recorded in an annotation before the first write, restored from it, annotation removed
2.live: yes, scripts/kind_bench.sh and omni_controller (HPA target, KEDA, Goldilocks, CruiseKube), three-run tables in results/live

3.name: Container Resources
3.native: the pod's own resource requests and limits (the Deployment template) and, where it runs, the VPA, Goldilocks or CruiseKube recommender
3.read: each pod's CPU use (kubectl top), its request and limit, the node's allocatable CPU (Kubernetes API)
3.write: the running pod's CPU limit in place through pods/resize (no restart); the template is never changed, so no rollout
3.restore: the operator's limit recorded in an annotation before the first write; every pod returned to it
3.live: yes, omni_controller/muscles.py convey() (conveyance); KEDA and Goldilocks tables

4.name: Kubernetes Placement & Scheduling
4.native: kube-scheduler and its profiles, the descheduler, PriorityClasses, scheduling gates
4.read: pods pending and their reasons, node fill, topology spread (Kubernetes API)
4.write: a pod's or deployment's placement fields (nodeSelector, affinity, topologySpreadConstraints, priorityClassName, schedulingGates) by kubectl patch, or the scheduler's profile
4.restore: the fields as they stood before the first write, restored field by field
4.live: modelled; the API path is the same kubectl patch the live controller uses for the HPA

5.name: Node Fleet & Karpenter-Class Control
5.native: the cluster's own node autoscaler: Karpenter (NodePool), the Cluster Autoscaler, a MachineSet, a cloud node pool
5.read: ready and schedulable workers, pending pods, allocatable and used CPU (Kubernetes API), the autoscaler's status ConfigMap
5.write: the pool's size through the operator's own command (--node-scale-cmd: az aks nodepool scale, gcloud container clusters resize, eksctl scale nodegroup, kubectl scale machineset, a Karpenter NodePool limit); a machine parked by taint and drain, never deleted by Omni-Compass
5.restore: the pool's starting count recorded once; every parked machine untainted and the pool restored to it at the end or on the lease
5.live: yes, omni_controller nodepool mode on kind and on AKS (results/live/V1_AKS_*, the capacity and steady tables)

6.name: OpenShift & Machine API

6.read: machine phases, MCP status and pause, degraded counts (the OpenShift API)
6.write: MachineHealthCheck maxUnhealthy, MachineConfigPool paused and maxUnavailable by oc patch
6.restore: the fields recorded before the first write, restored from the record
6.live: modelled; written against the documented OpenShift API, not yet run live

7.name: Cloud VM & Capacity
7.native: the cloud's autoscaling group or scale set: AWS Auto Scaling, Azure VMSS, GCP MIG
7.read: group size, instance states, the target-tracking metric (the cloud's API and monitoring)

8.name: Host CPU & Memory
8.native: the Linux kernel's own governors: cpufreq (schedutil or the processor driver), RAPL, cpuidle, the memory manager
8.read: /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq (frequencies and governor), /sys/class/powercap intel-rapl energy counters, /proc/stat busy share, /proc/pressure

terms.def: The gauge moved toward its declared aim against native: more work done, a shorter wait, fewer misses or failures, or a resource cut. Decided by what the gauge is for, never by the plus or minus sign of its number; its size is printed without a sign (GAIN 73.0%), the raw change apart with its true sign. terms.def: A change under 0.5% (the mean of the three runs' changes under the floor), no change at all, or a knob native already runs at the top of its range (at its limit on native). A change of 0.5% or more is never STEADY. Of three kinds: exactly the same (to nine decimal places), under the floor (a measured change under 0.5%), and, in a table read by an older key, no difference beyond the noise. Its size is printed without a sign (STEADY 0.3%), the raw change apart. S.T.E.A.D.Y.: Stable, True to baseline, Equilibrium, At par, Drift-free, Yield held. Yellow, and the yellow of the traffic signal on every monitor carries the same word.

terms.def: Every monitor's light, read on its band: green GAINING, low in its band with room to climb; yellow STEADY, inside its band; red REDLINING, at the top of its band and holding there, blinking red and black; red OVER THE LINE, past its band, blinking red and white; grey, and said so, where there is no line. On a record the colour is the reading's word: GAIN green, STEADY yellow, LOSS red. A needle that falls is not a LOSS and one that rises is not a GAIN: each light reads what its gauge is for. The light moves with its monitor: it reads the series the monitor draws. Every signal shows all four live words, the lit one bright and the rest dim, on native's side and on Omni-Compass's side alike: Omni-Compass's redline reflex is built never to let a muscle redline, and the red is still wired, so that if one does (a fault, a bug) it is seen at once, and the kill switch hands everything back to native in the same instant. The engine that stands carries the rule in its immune system, knob by knob, landed on 25 October (omnicompass/immune.py and its C++ twin cpp/src/immune.cpp): over its line three decisions, stuck, and native's twin lower by more than 5%, the knob is handed to native for 10 decisions, doubling up to 160; where native is not stronger Omni-Compass stays. The page's live model applies the same rule, with the engine's own numbers, to every muscle it draws.
